speaker: Doctor
text:
The mention of pale skin and multiple pinpoint, non-blanching red spots on your extremities is concerning; these could indicate petechiae associated with low platelets or a vascular issue. Given your age and the presence of these skin findings alongside fatigue, have you noticed any bleeding gums, blood in your stool, or unusual bruising?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count and Peripheral Smear.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology close-up of extremities.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 8.3 g/dL (low); WBC: 81,000 /mm3 (elevated); Platelets: 35,600 /mm3 (low); Peripheral Blood Smear Findings: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL). The combination of severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 35,600), extreme leukocytosis (WBC 81,000), and the specific presence of Auer rods (pink, needle-shaped inclusions) on the smear is pathognomonic for this life-threatening emergency. Given the risk of catastrophic hemorrhage, please proceed immediately with STAT coagulation studies (fibrinogen, PT/PTT) and start ATRA therapy.
